planting.note: Plant hardwood cuttings in spring in sandy, gravelly, well-drained soil in full sun; sand grape naturally grows on exposed gravel bars and rocky streambanks in the south-central US, so it tolerates lean, fast-draining sites poorly suited to most grapes.

directions: Plant in sandy, gravelly, well-drained soil in full sun; sand grape is a compact, shrubby wild grape native to gravel bars and rocky streambanks across the south-central United States, distinguished from most other native grapes by its low, bushy, non-climbing to weakly climbing habit and small, glossy, coarsely toothed leaves. The small, dark purple-black berries are tart and seedy, generally more valuable to wildlife and home winemakers blending with sweeter grapes than for fresh eating on their own. Its greatest significance is historical and genetic: sand grape's exceptional drought tolerance and resistance to grape phylloxera made it one of the key wild American species used to breed phylloxera-resistant rootstock in the late 19th century, helping save European wine grape production after the phylloxera epidemic devastated Old World vineyards. In the garden or native planting, it is a tough, low-maintenance vine well suited to lean, sandy, or rocky sites where other grapes struggle, and it provides food and cover for wildlife.
sources: University of California Cooperative Extension — Grape Rootstock History
